That's not how copyright works. The question is not whether you can use it, it's whether it's okay for people to edit it and then post an edited version - that's a derivative work, and violates copyright unless the author gives permission for it to be done.
If there's a bug and it can be fixed, it might be as simple as telling you to edit one line, or providing a separate plugin you'd include underneath this - but going off of what you think and guess isn't correct
As to your question:

2 - I don't entirely understand "half inverted" - nothing looks upside down to me. It looks to me in your screenshots like it's looping, is that correct? When there's empty room at the top, it's using that to display the portion of the map that's going off the bottom?

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
That screenshot makes it seem the small map size is the issue. Then the fix is easy: Make your maps bigger.
Once you made your map larger, you can select the map in the list, press CTRL+T to shift the actual area to the center.
Now you can choose to keep that new area empty, or fill it in with scenery and actually enlarge the map..
The trick now is to find out how large a map needs to be, for the mini-map to work correctly.
Edit: I don't know how effective a minimap is on a world-map of this size, though. If I were you I would disable it on the world map, and only use it in the area scenes, which are most likely larger areas anyway. If this is even possible.

Bingo! Thanks, ATT_Turan and JohnDoeNews, I analyzed the maps that work normally and those where this problem occurs. It’s definitely the map size; the issue happens with smaller maps.
If anyone is looking for a solution for this plugin, here’s a tip:
Solution for the proSnapMinimap plugin:
Minimum map size 27x18 (using a plugin for 1280x720 resolution). If you’re using the default RPG Maker MV resolution, test it out, but generally, avoid using smaller maps.
Aerosys, I just tested your MK_Minimap_Lite.js plugin, and it worked well—really good!
